In this lesson, you will learn about the operation of RC coupled transistor amplifiers.
INTRODUCTIONM
RC coupling is the most common method used to connect a multistage amplifier.
Both Q1 and Q2 are common emitter amplifiers. You know how they operate individually.
However, cascading Q1 and Q2 changes some circuit values.
Let's begin the lesson on RC COUPLED TRANSISTOR OPERATION...................
LESSON MENU
RC COUPLED TRANSISTOR AMPS
Circuit operation of RC coupled multistage amplifiers is very similar to circuit operation of individual amplifiers.
DISCUSSION
The only difference is that multistage amplifiers are connected and one stage affects the other.
For example, verifying normal operation of an individual amplifier requires comparing measured and calculated voltage gains.
Verifying normal operation of a multistage amplifier requires comparing TOTAL measured and calculated voltage gains.

Due to multistage amplifiers having at least two stages, the characteristics of an input signal become very important.
As the input frequency decreases, the reactances of C1, C3 and C5 increase.
For example, at 10 kHz, if C3 is a 10 mF capacitor, its AC resistance is 1.6 W.
For example, at 10 kHz, if C3 is a 10 mF capacitor, its AC resistance is 1.6 W......
Definition
The reactance is so small that it will not affect the circuit.
However, at 10 Hz, C3's reactance is 1.6 kW. The reactance is large and affects the circuit.
However, at 10 Hz, C3's reactance is 1.6 k ohms. The reactance is large and effects the circuit.
Definition
The large reactance decreases the total gain of the RC coupled amplifier. The individual stage gains are not affected; they're between the coupling capacitors.
For example, assume the Av of Q1 and Q2 is 10 (100 total) and C1, C3 and C5 reactances are high due to low frequency.
A 10 mVpp signal applied as an input produces an 8 mVpp signal on the base of Q1. C1 drops 2 mVpp.
With Q1 having a gain of 10, the output voltage is 80 mVpp on the collector. The individual stage operates normally.
If C3 drops 10 mVpp due to its reactance, the input to Q2 is 70 mVpp.
With Q2 having a gain of 10, the output voltage is .7 Vpp on the collector. The individual stage operates normally.
If C5 drops .1 Vpp due to its reactance, the output of the circuit is .6 Vpp.
Comparing the input voltage with the output voltage, the RC coupled amplifier circuit has a measured voltage gain of 60.
Each stage's voltage gain is good, but due to the reactances of the coupling capacitors, the total voltage gain is low and the circuit is not operating normally.
Also, if the input signal frequency is high, the gain of the amplifier is reduced.
The reduction in gain is caused by the transistors not being able to amplify signals above a certain frequency.
Each type of transistor has different characteristics; therefore, each type of transistor reduces the voltage gain at different high frequency points.
The amplitude of the input signal also effects circuit operation.
If the input signal is too large, Vpp, the output becomes distorted due to clipping.
The input signal drives Q1 into cutoff and saturation. Its output is clipped.
The total gain of the circuit is reduced and the output is distorted.
Or, Q1 stage may operate normally, but the Q2 stage clips the signal.
The result is still a reduced total gain with a distorted output signal.
In an RC coupled transistor amplifier, what is the result of a low frequency input signal?
stage gains good, total gain low, output signal distortedd
stage gains low, total gain low, output signal undistortedd
stage gains good, total gain low, output signal undistortedd
An input signal that is low in frequency does not distort the output signal. The coupling capacitors have high reactances that affect total gain.

stage gains low, total gain low, output signal undistortedd
stage gains good, total gain low, output signal undistortedd
stage gains low, total gain low, output signal distortedd
An input signal that has high Vpp causes the transistor to reach saturation and cutoff. This will affect the shape of the output signal.
